problems: southern-song is merged into northern-song (one state, Wikidata Q7462, both Cliopatria Names in cliopatria_names); there is no southern-song dossier, so the seed slug southern-song must map to northern-song. Other dossiers (mongol-empire, ngo-dynasty) cite southern-song as a counterpart.
Cliopatria's song (-750..-285) and xia (410..438) rows share Wikidata ids Q7462 and Q7427 with the Song and Western Xia dynasties but are different states.

Vassal events belong to the suzerain's dossier with the vassal as counterpart. Dossiers of other groups still need: uyghur-khaganate vassal pair 755-840 with khitan-confederation; mongol-empire vassal pairs with eastern-xia (1216-1217, 1218-1222) and eastern-liao (1212-1269); a counter-record of the Khitan rebellion of 696-714 in tang-dynasty. liao-dynasty carries the Jurchen vassal pair (1074 at confidence 1, 1114-09) and great-jin the Song, Goryeo, Xia and Qi pairs.
The goryeo dossier names the Jurchen counterpart 'jurchens' (993, 1104, 1107, 1108); the 1104-1108 events match jurchen-confederation, the 993 event predates it.
Dali's nominal Song tribute (982) is not recorded as vassal events (the page says 'essentially an independent state' and Cliopatria has no relation row).

Date conflicts between pages and other dossiers: Xiliangfu ends 1016 in xiliangfu.json but the Xia page has it annexed in 1032 (the xiliangfu dossier says its page lists Tsongkha as a successor, which the Tsongkha page does not say); Guiyi about 1030 (Xia page) against 1036; Qingtang 1113 (Song-Xia wars page) against 1108 and 1136 (Tsongkha page); Southern Tang 975 or 976; Dachanghe/Datianxing/Dayining 902/903-927, 928-929, 929-937 (Nanzhao page) against 927-928, 928-937 (Dali page); Yelu Liuge's revolt 1211 (Eastern Xia page) or 1212; Tsongkha ends 1103 (conquest) or 1104 (infobox); the Dali end is 1253 (infobox), 1256 (surrender) or 1259 (Cliopatria).

Cliopatria rows: Northern Song 1126 keeps the north after the Jin conquest; Western Xia 1216 drops the Hexi corridor ten years early and the row ends 1226; Great Jin 1216 and 1227 shapes run to 1235 although the Jin ended on 9 February 1234, and Manchuria vanishes in 1216 without a successor shape (now eastern-xia and eastern-liao); the Liao row starts 911 and has no Sixteen Prefectures transfer; Dali has four near-identical shapes running to 1259 that cover about 99% of Yunnan's area with different edges.

Two dossiers I wrote earlier were patched after later work: great-jin (the 1215 Manchuria loss raised from confidence 1 to 3 with the Eastern Xia page) and liao-dynasty (the Jurchen vassal pair added); both re-validated and read back from the mount.

Great Qi has no Wikipedia article (a red link on the Jin-Song wars page); its extent is a reading shared with the great-jin dossier. Great Chu's pages give Jiankang as capital, which conflicts with the other pages; its shape is a Kaifeng disc.
